thread:
alex: Quick heads-up — profiler during canary showed KV cache growth correlated with large continuous batches. hit soft OOM on one host, traced to batch formation admitting long-token requests back-to-back.
jin: Can you paste the snippet from the trace? which metrics spiked?
alex: pasted below (from host-23, 1:10pm):
```
free_kv_bytes: 1.1GB -> 420MB (within 120s)
batch_window_tokens: avg 1600
admitted_batch_tokens (single batch): 2300
kv_alloc_total: 4.3GB
oom_events: 1 (soft, reclaimed after eviction)
```
maya: OK. two quick ideas: 1) introduce a per-batch "token-budget gate" that clamps admitted token count when free_kv_bytes < THRESHOLD, and 2) a reroute policy to smaller quantized model for overflow. both lightweight. :thought_balloon:
chris: FWIW, last week's kernel swap (vectorized attention v2) is likely amplifying this — it reduces compute time but added an extra KV copy path which increases transient KV memory use. need kernel-selection guard too.
selena: Proposal: kv-aware hold queue. when free_kv_bytes < 800MB, long-context requests go into a 50ms hold queue (soft delay) to allow KV eviction + batching smoothing. if still low, reroute to "dedicated-small" pool or quantized fallback. record counters: hold_count, reroute_count, avg_hold_ms.
alex: I like the soft delay tread. fewer hard evictions. Also add a kernel switch rule: only enable v2 kernel for batches with admitted tokens < 1200 and per-request kv_size_estimate < 300KB.
jin: Can we compute kv_size_estimate cheaply? maybe estimate = request_context_len * per_token_kv_bytes (heuristic) and update from recent samples.
maya: yes, cheap estimate works fine as gate. We'll also expose config knobs: free_kv_threshold_mb, token_budget_cap, hold_ms, reroute_pool.
chris: quick note on perf/regressions — if we gate kernel v2 too aggressively we lose compute benefit. plan: multi-arm AB: (A) kernel v2 unchanged, (B) kernel v2 gated by token budget, (C) kernel v2 + reroute fallback. measure P50/P90 latency and cache-eviction rate. run 6h per arm.
selena: I'll instrument the metrics + add tracing spans: batch.admit_reason, batch.token_budget, kernel.choice, reroute.target. Also add alert when reroute_rate > 1% over 10m.
ci-bot: deploy started: feature/kv-batch-gates -> staging (build #4021).
alex: thanks @selena, @maya — once deployed let's run a short canary on the saturated host group and compare KV tail behaviour. If hold queue reduces soft OOMs without hurting P90 by >10% we keep.
jin: small nit — ensure the fallback pool has identical tokenization & compat model signature to avoid inference errors.
maya: noted. I'll sketch the config and open a PR with tests + perf dashboard by EOD.
chris: +1. also add a microbenchmark to measure the extra KV copy cost of kernel v2 when batch tokens ~2k. want numbers before gating defaults.
alex: cool. action items: maya = PR + config, selena = metrics + alerts, chris = microbench, jin = verify fallback model compatibility. I'll run the AB and post results here. :rocket:
